title: ExoHub provenance record
description: Compact record profile for ExoHub provenance records (design D2, D4): the envelope (context IRI, @id urn:exohub:record:<UUIDv7>, exo:assertion enum, exo:assertedBy, generatedAtTime, non-empty @graph), exo:supersedes, node @type/property term set, and the prefixed-extension shape. It does NOT check that referenced content ids exist in a repository, cross-record conflicts (duplicate ids, unknown supersedes, conflicting single-valued properties), immutability of committed records, or that a node's "prefix:local" property uses a prefix actually declared in the record's own @context object (a cross-field check) — those require the repository, git history, or the record's own context, and are checked by `exo provenance validate` and `exo bundle`.

context.description: The context IRI alone, or the context IRI plus an additional context object declaring extension prefixes (design D2: additional properties SHALL use a prefix declared in an additional context object). Declared prefix names are checked against the reserved list (see reservedContextName) directly in this schema. This schema cannot see which prefixes a record declares when checking a node's "prefix:local" properties (prefixed node properties are only pattern-checked, see node.patternProperties) — the exo/internal/provenance Go package (isReservedContextName, ValidateContextPrefixes) enforces that a used prefix was actually declared here.

reservedContextName.description: The reserved names an additional context object's prefix must not redefine (design D2): the four namespace prefixes the embedded context declares, plus every unprefixed node type and property alias. This enum MUST match provenance.isReservedContextName in exo/internal/provenance/context.go exactly.

nodeType.description: An unprefixed node type alias declared by the embedded context (design D1); see provenance.NodeTypeIRI.

node.description: A PROV node in @graph. Property keys are restricted to @id, @type, the unprefixed context property aliases, and "prefix:local" keys (design D2); the Go package additionally requires "prefix:local" keys to resolve against exo: or a prefix the record declares in its context object.
